title: Feedback and status components: alerts, banners, empty, loading, error, skeleton
asA: user needing to know what the application is doing and what needs attention
iWant: status surfaces that inform without shouting or disappearing
soThat: I trust the application to tell me the truth about its state

acceptanceCriteria.description: Alerts render the four semantic intents (info, success, warning, danger) from the token layer with intent icons from the semantic alias registry, in both themes.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an alert of each intent in each theme
acceptanceCriteria.then: intent styling and icon are correct and token-driven

acceptanceCriteria.description: Alerts announcing dynamic outcomes use a live region appropriate to urgency; page-load-present alerts are static content.
acceptanceCriteria.given: an alert raised by a user action
acceptanceCriteria.then: assistive technology announces it without focus theft

acceptanceCriteria.description: Banners occupy the shell-owned banner slot, never overlap content, push layout rather than cover it, and are dismissible where the condition is not persistent.
acceptanceCriteria.then: content reflows below it and dismissal follows the declared rule

acceptanceCriteria.description: The empty-state component renders an illustration or icon, a headline naming what would be here, and the primary action that fills it, per the empty-state wireframe.
acceptanceCriteria.then: all three elements are present and the action works

acceptanceCriteria.description: Skeleton loaders mirror the shape of the incoming content, animate within motion-token constraints, respect reduced motion, and are marked busy for assistive technology.
acceptanceCriteria.given: a loading collection with known shape
acceptanceCriteria.then: its silhouette matches the loaded layout and it exposes busy state

acceptanceCriteria.description: The error-state component names what failed in user terms, offers a retry or an alternative path, and never renders a raw exception, stack trace, or internal id.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the copy is actionable per spa-REQ-017 and a retry affordance is present

acceptanceCriteria.description: Spinners appear only for genuinely indeterminate operations, always paired with an accessible label naming what is loading.
acceptanceCriteria.then: the spinner has an accessible name and is not used where a skeleton was possible
